meanings.note: imperative держи! when handing something over
imperative держи! when handing something over
Secondary conversational sense ('catch!, grab (him)!') (держи его!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Here you go, this is for you.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'fish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: comparative крепче = tighter, more firmly
Secondary conversational sense ('soundly') (крепко спать = sleep soundly) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотри, держи меня за ногу. Вот так! Крепче держи!
examples.trans: Look, hold me by the leg. Like that! Hold tighter!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'almost'.

examples.text: Наш с вами город очень старый. Почти четыре века здесь были набеги.
examples.trans: Our town is very old. For almost four centuries there were raids here.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come', forming an aspectual pair with 'приходить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'идти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'neighboring' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: В соседнем зале играет тихая музыка.
examples.trans: Quiet music plays in the neighboring hall.

examples.text: За соседним столиком сидели приятные люди.
examples.trans: Pleasant people were sitting at the next table.
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'more'.
Secondary conversational sense ('bigger') (comparative of большой) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: + dative + infinitive: мне терять нечего = I have nothing to lose

examples.trans: There is nothing to do here.

examples.text: Ты знаешь, что я хочу. Мне терять нечего.
examples.trans: You know what I want. I have nothing to lose.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to prepare') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'not bad', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Это на самом деле неплохой вариант.
examples.trans: This is actually not a bad option.

examples.text: У него неплохой голос для пения.
examples.trans: He has a fairly good singing voice.
They say they cook pretty good dishes there.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Abstract feminine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'nonsense'.
Secondary conversational sense ('stupidity, foolishness') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Что за глупости? Значит, Осипенко сам эти деньги украл!
examples.trans: What nonsense? That means Osipenko stole that money himself!

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun
Secondary conversational sense ('alone') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: рассказывай! = tell me (your news)!

examples.trans: So, tell me, how are you doing?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'food', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: В этом ресторане всегда свежая еда.
examples.trans: There is always fresh food in this restaurant.
Oh no, bad food? Does your stomach hurt?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'probably'.

examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.
He has probably already come home.

examples.text: Наверное, что-то серьёзное у вас. Девочка уже две недели лежит в областной клинике!
examples.trans: It must be something serious for you. The girl has been lying in the regional clinic for two weeks already!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'right', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('right, correct') (short form: ты прав = you're right) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Secondary conversational sense ('better') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'town, city' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: almost always the short form: я согласен (man), я согласна (woman)

examples.text: Я полностью согласен с вашим предложением по новому меню!
examples.trans: I completely agree with your proposal for the new menu!

examples.text: Все повара были согласны остаться вечером и помочь шефу.
examples.trans: All the cooks agreed to stay in the evening and help the chef.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: сто пятьдесят = a hundred and fifty; сто рублей = a hundred roubles

examples.trans: I've got a hundred and ten.

examples.text: Понимаешь, Аркаша, мы все скидываемся на этот кластер. Мне москвичам сегодня надо отдать сто пятьдесят.
examples.trans: You see, Arkasha, we're all chipping in for this cluster. I have to give the Moscow people a hundred and fifty today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'цент'). Common masculine noun meaning 'percent, interest rate' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('interest rate') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Они накрутили со своими бандитскими процентами.
examples.trans: They piled it on with their gangster interest rates.
A loan at a low interest rate.

examples.text: А они накрутили со своими бандитскими процентами.
examples.trans: And they piled it on with their gangster interest rates.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('expression') (to run for a second term) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.
